planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants after all frost danger has passed, since this East African shrub has no cold tolerance and is grown as a perennial only in warm climates or as a container specimen elsewhere.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to light shade, watering regularly during establishment and allowing some drying between waterings once mature. This East African shrub produces its namesake flowers in a striking bicolor pattern: a hooded orange-red corolla emerges from a pair of black-maroon calyx lobes that resemble an open jaw, a combination that makes it a favorite nectar source for sunbirds and hummingbirds in cultivation. Prune lightly after flowering flushes to maintain a compact, bushy habit, since the plant can become loose and sprawling if left unchecked. It tolerates heat and brief dry spells well once established but should be protected from frost and from waterlogged soil.
sources: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew — Plants of the World Online
